notes.decision: Translated 'these two trees, originating from one another' — but lines 2-3 then deny this proposition ('they did not become from one another'). Reading the sequence as the question/thesis being refuted: the two trees (good and evil) do NOT share a common origin. Lycopolitan ⲛ̄ⲯ- = circumstantial 'as they...' or conjunctive prefix.

ⲡⲁⲣⲭⲟⲩ from Greek ὑπάρχω 'subsist, originate.' The relative ⲉⲧⲁ- introduces the contrast: 'rather, they originate (each from its own root).' The two trees of Manichaean cosmology — Tree of Life and Tree of Death — have entirely separate origins in the two principles.
ⲉⲯⲍⲁⲩ = ⲉϥϩⲁⲩ 'evil/bad.' Standard Manichaean trope: the evil tree produces the evil fruit; the good tree the good fruit. Each tree manifests according to its own root.
The doxological closing formula ϣⲁ ⲉⲛⲏϩ ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ ⲛⲉⲛⲏϩ 'forever and ever' (εἰς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων). Lycopolitan ⲏⲍⲉ for ⲏϩⲉ. This marks the close of the previous chapter on the two trees.

ⲧⲍⲉⲣⲙⲏⲛⲓⲁ = Greek ἑρμηνεία 'interpretation, explanation.' ⲧⲉⲩⲁⲁⲙⲟⲛⲓⲁ = Greek εὐδαιμονία 'eudaimonia, blessedness, prosperity.' Retained as 'Eudaimonia' to preserve the technical Greek philosophical loanword that the Coptic itself uses; the chapter goes on to map worldly Eudaimonia (with worldly Sophia and Dynamis) onto its divine counterpart, the Father in the great land of Light.
ⲧⲟⲁⲙ = Lycopolitan reflex of ⲧϭⲟⲙ 'the Power' (Greek δύναμις). Together with Sophia (Wisdom), these form the worldly triad alongside Eudaimonia which the chapter will compare to the divine triad.

Greek loanword φωστήρ 'luminary, light-bearer.' Standard Manichaean title for Mani himself (the Apostle of Light). Translated 'the Illuminator' to preserve the active light-giving function (per correspondential principle: a title from light-emission stays verbal).
ⲍⲙⲁⲥⲧ = ⲉϥϩⲙⲟⲟⲥ 'while sitting/seated.' ⲧⲥⲁⲩⲍⲉ̄ = ⲧⲥⲱⲟⲩϩⲥ 'the assembly, gathering, congregation.' Standard scene-setting: Mani teaching seated in the Church assembly.

ⲟⲩⲉⲓⲛⲉ here is the verb 'to pass by, transit' (Sah. ⲟⲩⲉⲓⲛⲉ/ⲟⲩⲱⲧⲃ), NOT the noun 'likeness.' Context (the Eudaimonia of the world is transient): 'she passes by/passes away.' The worldly Eudaimonia is contrasted with the abiding divine Eudaimonia of the Father.

Obscure verbal form. Possibly a Lycopolitan compound involving ⲥⲉⲃⲟ-/ⲥⲃⲱ ('teaching/instruction') with feminine subject, or a Greek-derived verb (perhaps from συμβοήθεια 'mutual aid' or related). Tentatively translated 'is paired-with' to fit the parallel context (Sophia is set 'beside' another Sophia in line 27/segment 27, ⲟⲱⲗ ⲁⲍⲁⲛ 'stands beside'). Requires further philological investigation.
ⲟⲱⲗ likely Lycopolitan for ⲱϩⲉ 'stand'; ⲁⲍⲁⲛ = ⲁϩⲏⲛ 'near, beside'; ⲕⲉⲟⲁⲙ = ⲕⲉϭⲟⲙ 'another Power.' Reading: 'stands beside another Power,' the structural parallel to the Sophia clause.

ⲡⲁ-ⲡⲉⲁⲩ 'the one of glory' = 'the glorious one.' The Eudaimonia of the glorious one IS the Father, the God [of Truth]. The text identifies — does not compare — the divine Eudaimonia with the Father himself. This is correspondential identity at the highest register.
ⲡⲛⲁⲟ ⲛⲕⲁⲍ = ⲡⲛⲟϭ ⲛⲕⲁϩ 'the great land/earth.' Standard Manichaean term for the Land of Light, the Father's own dwelling. ⲥⲙⲁⲛⲧ = qualitative of ⲥⲙⲛⲧ 'be founded, established.'
